newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Westa offers Prochnik stake sale.
newsitem.headline: Polish Westa offers Prochnik stake sale.

text.p: The receiver of the bankrupt Polish insurer Westa subscribed to sell her 15.4-percent-stake in garment maker Prochnik SA in the public tender offer called by National Investment Fund (NFI) No.12, the receiver said.
Dorota Brzezinska-Grabarczyk told Reuters on Tuesday, the transaction could be carried out on the Warsaw bourse by April 8, but said the offer might be reduced if supply was greater than demand.
"We have subscribed to sell 230,882 shares, the whole stake we have in Prochnik, in the public tender offer," she said.
Westa receiver cuts her original 25-percent stake in Prochnik to 15.4 percent after an early-February sale of 149,999 shares, or 9.9 percent of the garment maker to NFI 12.
Last month NFI 12 announced a public tender offer to buy 343,501 Prochnik shares at 11 zlotys per share to up its stake to 32.9 percent.
NFI 12 is one of the 15 NFIs in Poland's mass privatisation scheme in which the funds hold stakes and manage about 500 companies.
